result.summary: Sutskever's dated 2017 predictions are all in private emails to Elon Musk that OpenAI published in December 2024. The June 12 email gives one-month (Dota 1v1) and six-month (robot hand) targets. The July 12 email ('The business of building AGI') gives three-year goals (robotics solved, theorem proving, programming competitions, chatbots), a chance of AGI in as little as four years with the algorithm 2-4 years later, and a promise to solve adversarial examples by the end of August. His public remarks found for 2017 hold only an undated comment that AGI 'seems far off right now'.

reply_text:
I found five dated predictions in Sutskever's 2017 words. All of them come from his private emails to Elon Musk, which OpenAI later published, and none from anything he said in public that year. Every quote below is copied from the page I opened, OpenAI's December 2024 post "Elon Musk wanted an OpenAI for-profit". That page shows both emails as "From: Ilya Sutskever", but the July 12 one is written as "we" and appears to speak for him and Greg Brockman too.

**June 12, 2017 email ("Bi-weekly updates"):**
- Dota 2: the bot would win the 1v1 version of the game within a month.
- Robotics: within six months OpenAI would do at least one of three hand tasks (one-handed Rubik's cube, pen spinning or spinning Chinese balls).

**July 12, 2017 email ("The business of building AGI"):**
- Within three years: robotics completely solved, AI proving a long-standing unproven theorem, AIs winning programming competitions consistently, and convincing chatbots (though none passing the Turing test).
- AGI: in as little as four years there would be "an actual chance of waking up to AGI", and the algorithm would be found within two to four more years after that.
- Adversarial examples: the email's progress notes say the problem would be completely solved "by the end of August".

**Left out by your rules:** the same email forecasts deep learning hardware speeding up 10x a year for four to five years, and says AGI could be built with less than $10B in hardware. Those are hardware and spending forecasts. The GPU and headcount plans are business forecasts. A July 21 path through "end of 2017" was written by Brockman, not Sutskever.

**Public statements:** In March 2017 at the EmTech Digital conference he said AGI "seems far off right now". I only saw that in an MIT Technology Review report, and it has no date, so it is under undated. The "Honest thoughts" email of September 20, 2017 has no dated AI prediction. His December 2017 Fields Institute talk exists only as video, and I didn't find a transcript of his NIPS 2017 talk, so I could check neither. The OpenAI page itself opened fine; the LessWrong copy of the emails cut off before 2017, and one news page (inkl) would not open.
